additional_context:
[Council feedback on the previous definition]
From model_reviewer:
- proposed_definition.kinematic_profile.primary_joint_actions[elbow_joint/flexion]: Elbow flexion is counted at full weight, so brachialis, both biceps heads and brachioradialis become primary movers. The source instructions say to avoid using the biceps and to treat the arms as hooks, with the rear delts doing the work. The frames show the elbow bending as the bar rises, so the joint does move, but it is a minor contributor rather than a load-moving action. The assumption that 'biceps involvement is the elbow flexion needed to hold the bar path' also conflicts with the primary emphasis the output reflects. Suggested correction: Keep elbow_joint/flexion but mark it emphasis 'assist'. This makes the elbow flexors synergists at 0.4 x table weight (brachialis 0.4, biceps heads 0.32, brachioradialis 0.28) and leaves rear deltoid, rhomboids and transverse trapezius as the primary movers.
- engaged_muscles_by_role.primary: Because of the elbow-flexion emphasis, brachialis, brachioradialis, long head of biceps brachii and short head of biceps brachii (left and right) are listed as primary. This contradicts the stated rear-delt focus and 'refrain from using your biceps' cue, so the resulting tracer profile is wrong for this exercise. Suggested correction: After setting elbow flexion to assist, these muscles should appear as synergists and not as primary movers.
[End of council feedback]

assumptions: The exercise is bilateral and counted by repetitions.
Elbow flexion is marked assist because the cues say to use the arms as hooks and not to use the biceps. The elbow still bends as the bar rises in the frames.
Horizontal abduction at the glenohumeral joint with scapular retraction drives the pull, matching the cue to keep the upper arms perpendicular to the torso and squeeze the rear delts.

The torso is held roughly parallel to the floor with a neutral spine. The hip extensors and spinal erectors work isometrically, so hip extension is an assist action and anti_flexion_spine is a demand.
The hands are the free distal segment moving the bar, so the chain is classified as open_chain.
The bar is held in the hands, so grip and wrist_stability apply.
classification_reasons: The frames and instructions show a bilateral bent-over barbell row with a wide overhand grip, elbows flared, and the bar pulled toward the upper chest.
Every joint action and stabilization demand needed is available in the tracer vocabulary.

instructions: Stand up straight while holding a barbell using a wide (higher than shoulder width) and overhand (palms facing your body) grip.

Bend knees slightly and bend over as you keep the natural arch of your back. Let the arms hang in front of you as they hold the bar. Once your torso is parallel to the floor, flare the elbows out and away from your body. Tip: Your torso and your arms should resemble the letter "T". Now you are ready to begin the exercise.

While keeping the upper arms perpendicular to the torso, pull the barbell up towards your upper chest as you squeeze the rear delts and you breathe out. Tip: When performed correctly, this exercise should resemble a bench press in reverse. Also, refrain from using your biceps to do the work. Focus on targeting the rear delts; the arms should only act as hooks.
Slowly go back to the initial position as you breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
source.name: Barbell Rear Delt Row
